paper.title_en: Toward the first experiments of T-violation search in neutron-induced compound nuclear reaction
paper.abstract_en: In a low energy region, the CP violation beyond the standard model is explored as probing violating effects of time-reversal symmetry(T-violation) in various physics systems. Neutron-induced compound nuclear reactions are interesting because the enhancement of parity-nonconservation effect(PNC) has been found in many compound nuclear states. Particularly, a Lanthanum nucleus($^{139}$La) reaches the enhancement of $10^6$ at the P-resonance of 0.75 eV. This enhancement can be also expected for the T-violating effects from recent experimental results and theoretical calculations. Additionally, this system is sensitive to a different T-violating parameter from the neutron EDM. The NOPTREX (Neutron Optical Parity and Time Reversal Experiment) collaboration is addressing several experimental issues for the T-violation search with La solid targets as a first step. One big issue is the development of a polarized La target because polarized solid targets except for protons and deuterons have not been realized yet as a practical use. We give the overview of the T-violation search in the neutron-induced compound states, present the results of experiments in the base stage with a brute-force polarized target, and then report the current status of the first stage with a dynamically-polarized target, which we call Phase-1.
